messages:
maya: Quick update from the continuous-batching probe — ran rebalance + soft-reserve changes on staging clusters this AM. Fewer P99 spikes overall but noticed an oscillation pattern when several high-throughput tenants aligned on burst windows.
liam: What did you change for rebalance?
maya: Two main changes: 1) an asymmetric hysteresis (split fast, merge slow) and 2) a tiny soft-reserve credit that decays. Also added a token-cost gate to avoid splitting on many tiny short requests.
kai: How are you calculating token-cost? Per-request token estimate?
maya: We used a cheap estimator: length_tokens + estimated_response_tokens (based on model_profile). Its approximate but caught the pathological short-vs-long mixes.
oliver: Can you share the thresholds you experimented with?
maya: Pasted config snippet:
```
rebalance:
  split:
    queue_count: 100
    median_latency_ms: 55
    sustained_secs: 6
  merge:
    idle_secs: 120
soft_reserve:
  credits_ms_equiv: 12
  decay_ms: adaptive
token_gate:
  enabled: true
  token_cost_threshold: 180
```
liam: "decay_ms: adaptive" — how are we driving adaptivity?
maya: We compute decay = max(500, min(3000, kv_warmup_ms * 0.5)). Idea: long KV warmups => longer soft-reserve so tenant has time to warm caches after a shard move.
anya: That seems reasonable, but could extend tail if someone intentionally pads requests. Any guardrails?
maya: Yes, we cap credits and only apply soft-reserve for tenants with sustained_kv_miss_rate > 0.05.
kai: Observed routing churn when splits happen?
maya: Yup. routing_delta_rate spiked ~4x for ~20-40s after some splits, and neighbor shards saw short queue spikes. Thats the main source of the oscillation.
oliver: Can we smooth routing changes with a handoff window? Like drain-to-new-shard for a few inflight batches?
liam: That would reduce churn but complicate admission semantics. We may need a graceful-transfer handshake: allow inflight to complete and route new requests via a shadow-mirror for Xs while the shard stabilizes.
aya: (typo: meaning anya) We should be careful with API surface. Avoid blocking paths.
maya: Agreed. For now we added asymmetric hysteresis: split cooldown 30s, merge cooldown 180s to avoid flip-flops. Also limit split_rate per-cluster to baseline*2 per minute.
kai: Telemetry additions we need?
maya: Add per-tenant post-split warmup_histogram, routing_delta_rate, per-shard split_latency_impact, and token_cost_imbalance ratio.
oliver: Alerts?
maya: Alert conditions proposed: rolling P99 increase > 12% over 30m; split_rate > baseline*3 for 5m; routing_delta_rate > 50 changes/min sustained for 10m.
liam: What about admission interface changes? Are we adding hooks?
maya: Kept it minimal: scheduler now supports register_split_policy(name, config_blob) and register_soft_reserve_policy(name, config_blob). Defaults unset. No blocking sync hooks; callbacks run in control-plane async.
aya: For rollout, recommend canary flow with automatic rollback. What are rollback triggers?
maya: Canary for 24h on two clusters with auto-rollback if P99 > baseline*1.15 or split_rate > baseline*3 or routing_delta_rate alarm fires. Runbook will include manual escalation to eng-sre.
kai: Any CPU/GPU cost changes?
maya: Small: token-gate bookkeeping added ~1-2% CPU on control-plane, and slight extra RPCs during split (~2% token-cost during first minute). Noticed KV-cache priming increased memory churn on some nodes.
oliver: Action items?
maya: 1) liam: land token-cost gating + unit tests. 2) liam+maya: implement adaptive decay based on kv_warmup_ms and sustained_kv_miss_rate. 3) oliver: dashboards & routing_delta_rate alarm. 4) anya: review canary runbook and rollback steps. 5) kai: verify soft-reserve doesnt open QoS bypass in perf tests.
liam: I'll pick up the PR for token gating today.
aya: I'll read the runbook tonight.
kai: I'll run the perf matrix for soft-reserve scenarios.
sre-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: canary-control-plane-7 at 2025-07-19T14:00Z. Will post status updates. :robot_face:
maya: Thanks team. Will post the 6h and 24h telemetry snapshots here. :thumbsup:
